spec.name: architect-sees-the-design
spec.intent:
Worktree /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share (branch design/first-share); every path below is under it and no command runs in the main checkout. Census @f2cd7e3a: the design was corrected there; plan architect-position is stopped under `design stability` and its landed architect-role and architect-skills work (7d53132e, e944facb, 9809add3, c076a864, ce240336, 539140df) is this unit's starting state. Re-derive any count or line below if a listed path changed since. Realize the corrected `architect position` in the architect's role and its generic holder: the role holds the design and nothing below it, treats every input as a hypothesis to rectify, cuts shards for the planner, never sees a unit's spec, an implementation or an implementer's account, and routes each assay verdict (not achieved: to the same implementer with the findings; achieved: to the integrator).
THE LOOP (the contract the workflow units of this plan each state their own share of; the shards say what must hold, this is how). (1) The architect cuts a shard and dispatches the planner with it; the planner plans it and, when no plan is bound, binds it, returning only the plan's name. (2) The architect dispatches one integrator for the bound plan, named for the plan and kept warm across its waves where the harness can message a finished delegate (Claude Code: SendMessage to the name given at dispatch; omp: agent messaging); the integrator records each ready unit active as it hands out its address and returns only addresses, `<unit> of <plan>`. (3) The architect dispatches one implementer per address, naming the delegate after the unit and giving it the address and nothing it wrote itself. The implementer reads its spec, builds on its own branch, runs only its unit's own checks, commits its own work, and returns only `landed <unit> of <plan> at <commit>`, or `blocked <unit> of <plan>: spec` when the spec cannot be built as written (the architect routes that address to the planner). Its account of the work stays out of the return; what it doubts or meets beside the path it captures as a note. (4) The architect dispatches the assayer with the address and commit. The assayer reads the shard the unit realizes and the files at that commit, never the spec, and returns the assay verdict: achieved, or not achieved with what is missing in the design's own words, naming the unit and its implementer. (5) Not achieved: the architect sends the findings to the same implementer by the name it gave it, and the unit returns to (4). Achieved: the architect hands the address and commit to the integrator. (6) The integrator combines the unit onto the plan's integration line (a branch cut from main when the plan is bound, `plan/<plan>`) and runs the project's whole check once on the combined tree; no implementer or assayer runs it. Green: it records the unit completed, commits the records written since (plan, design, notes) by pathspec, and returns the unit as whole with the newly ready addresses. Red or a merge conflict: it leaves the line as it was and returns `red <unit> of <plan>: <failing check>`, which the architect sends to the same implementer. It never repairs, never reads to judge, and decides nothing. (7) When every unit is completed and the whole holds, the integrator closes the plan and asks the operator to release the line to main: a pull request where the repository has a forge remote and `gh`, otherwise the exact git command. It never moves main. (8) The architect never runs `plan show <unit>`, and never reads a spec, a diff, an artifact or an implementer's account; it runs no check and makes no commit or merge. Unit names reach it only as addresses, from the integrator and on verdicts. (9) Design stability. Every input, whether from the operator, a delegate or the architect itself, is a hypothesis the architect rectifies against its expertise and industry practice. A surviving change that bears on a shard the bound plan realizes is captured as a decision note on that concept's topic, blocking nothing; it is amended into the design only after that plan closes, and a following plan realizes it. A change to a concept no bound plan realizes is amended at once. Only when the architect finds the bound plan built on a shard that is itself wrong does it stop the plan: it captures a note blocking the plan (an owed ruling, so no unit is ready), corrects the shard once, and the planner rectifies the plan (repin, revise, retract, add) or rebuilds it; the architect then retracts the note and work resumes.
CHANGE. (1) packages/canon/src/dimensions/role/architect.ts, the `## Role` every holder projects. At census it reads `reads⟨intent · C · plan-view · note · assay · gate-result⟩ → writes⟨C · note · verdict⟩` and reserves `judge(assay)` and `DECISION accept(unit) ⟨judged ↾ ⟨assay · gate-result⟩⟩` and `DECISION bind(P)`. The corrected position takes the judgement away (the assayer's verdict is the acceptance) and the plan view (units reach it only as addresses). The arrow becomes reads⟨intent · C · note · verdict · address⟩ → writes⟨C · note · route⟩. reserves: author and amend C, rectify every input against expertise and industry practice (the operator's included), cut C into shards, route each verdict per (5) and each red per (6), stop a plan built on a wrong shard per (9). Keep the self-classifying delegation clause and `descent`. The routing line names planner, implementer, assayer and integrator.
(2) packages/canon/src/roles/architect.ts: `skills` becomes ['design', 'note']. deliver leaves because it composes the plan skill (census, slice, add, and `show <unit>`, the spec read) and because under the corrected design deliver is the integrator's skill (plan integrator-makes-whole and deliver-loop). This also answers note 'plan reaches architects through deliver' without breaking `skill routing`: the architect is given its role's skills with everything they compose, and they no longer compose plan. Rewrite the comments that say deliver 'closes the loop on what comes back', the objective comment's 'a position that integrates holds delivery' (keep conceptual-integrity), the principles comment 'what comes back is judged against the design rather than trusted' (the assayer judges now), and the selfEvaluation comment's 'acceptance is judged against the criteria' (acceptance rests on the verdict).
(3) packages/canon/src/dimensions/engineering-principles/trust-but-verify.ts, which only the architect holds, reads `trust-but-verify ⟨operator-intent exempt ⟨extracted · served · ¬verified⟩⟩`. That exemption contradicts the corrected position (the operator's input is a hypothesis to rectify like any other). Restate it with no exemption, the operator's input rectified before it is served.
(4) packages/canon/src/dimensions/role/implementer.ts gains the return clause of (3): return ≜ address ⟨landed ∨ blocked-on-spec⟩, the account stays out of it, a doubt or defect beside the path is a note.
(5) packages/canon/src/dimensions/actions/delegation.ts (architect and nico hold it): keep every clause reader-reach.test.ts matches (`return ↦ σ*`, `¬long-form-prose`, `human-project ↾ carried-deliverable`, no `ρ=`) and the commit clause (writer commits its own unit work, the integrator commits merges and records, the dispatcher commits nothing); add that a dispatch carries an address and never a spec the dispatcher wrote, and that a delegate is named so it can be messaged again.
(6) packages/canon/src/hooks/purview-guardrail.ts. It blocks 'a dispatch to a builder for a piece no planner decomposed' and passes only 'a dispatch to a planner, a dispatch to an assayer' (header comment, `residue` `dispatch ↦ plan ∨ assay`, the denial `feedback`, and the rubric's 'What to PASS'). Under the loop the architect dispatches implementers and the integrator too, by address. Pass a dispatch to an implementer that carries a unit address and the planner's spec by reference, and a dispatch to the integrator; keep blocking a dispatch carrying a spec the dispatcher wrote itself or the operator's literal words. Then regenerate packages/canon/targets/guardrail/purview-guardrail.sh with `pnpm canon:project:targets` (cwd /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share); no other targets/ file may change. Update packages/canon/test/purview-guardrail.test.ts only where it asserts the old route text.
(7) packages/canon/src/agents/architect.ts, the generic subagent-oriented holder (operator ruling 'named personas and generic positions'). Its description says it 'judge[s] assays of what was built'; it becomes the corrected position: holds the design, cuts shards for planners, routes assay verdicts, hands planning, building, judging and making work whole to planner, implementer, assayer and integrator. The archetype drops what a cold read takes as judging or reading below the design.
(8) .changeset/architects-hold-the-design.md states the corrected position.
kino, mav and nico are wave-1 units (their files compile against roles/architect.ts). The integrator agent is created by integrator-makes-whole in this wave; this unit only names the role.

COLD READ. For each of architect, give its session text (RIG), with no other context and no tools, to anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 and anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 with this prompt verbatim: 'Below is the complete definition of an AI agent and the skills loaded into it at session start. Answer from this text alone, quoting the lines that decide each answer, with YES, NO or UNCLEAR where a question asks yes or no. (a) Does it itself build or edit product code or files, other than its own design records? (b) Does it itself run code, tests, builds or checks? (c) Does it itself commit or merge? (d) Does it itself read a unit's spec, a diff, a produced artifact, or an implementer's account of its work? (e) Does it itself decide whether a unit achieves what it was built for? (f) When the verdict on a unit comes back not achieved, what does it do and to whom? And when achieved? (g) While a plan is running, the operator asks for a change to something that plan is building. What does it do? (h) To whom, by name, does it hand planning, building, judging a unit against its goal, and combining approved work and running the full check?' Save every prompt and answer verbatim under /tmp/corrected-shards-cold-read/architect-sees-the-design/ and print the number of reads taken. PASSES when every read answers NO to (a) through (e); every (f) says not-achieved goes back to the same implementer with the findings and achieved goes to the integrator; every (g) says the change is weighed (rectified) and then waits to be realized by a following plan rather than amending what the running plan builds, unless the goal itself is wrong; every (h) names planner, implementer, assayer and integrator. A YES or UNCLEAR quoting a line this unit's outputs project fails it. FAILS at census: the census architect reserves `judge(assay)` and `DECISION accept(unit) ⟨judged ↾ ⟨assay · gate-result⟩⟩`, so (e) comes back YES, and it loads deliver, whose `finding ⇒ fold ≺ self's next dispatch` makes (g) an immediate amendment.
